newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Separatist leader to visit Georgia for first time.
newsitem.headline: Separatist leader to visit Georgia for first time.

text.p: The leader of Georgia's breakaway Abkhazia region was expected to arrive in the capital Tbilisi on Thursday for unprecedented face-to-face peace talks with President Eduard Shevardnadze, an official said.
Vakhtang Abashidze, spokesman for Shevardnadze, said Abkhaz leader Vladislav Ardzinba would come together with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, who has been mediating the talks.
Ardzinba's visit is the first to Georgia since he became leader of Abkhazia and comes five years to the day since Georgian troops entered the province to put down a move towards independence.

Talks between Georgia and Abkhazia on reaching a full political agreement have been deadlocked. The subtropical Black Sea region has run itself as a de facto independent state since the brutal 1992-93 ethnic conflict between the two sides in which some 10,000 people were killed.
Heavy security was in place around the city airport in advance of the arrival of Primakov and Ardzinba. Primakov's visit had been previously announced.
Primakov has said he hopes to prepare a deal between Georgia and Abkhazia to pave the way for a formal peace agreement to be signed in Moscow in the presence of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
